summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted following a two-hour episode of transient bilateral visual loss, accompanied by a severe vertex headache, bilateral temporal tenderness, jaw stiffness, and shoulder pain. Imaging showed no acute stroke but revealed chronic infarcts and vascular changes. Elevated ESR and clinical symptoms raised strong suspicion for giant cell arteritis. The patient was started on high-dose prednisone and famotidine, with adjustments to insulin therapy due to steroid-induced hyperglycemia. A temporal artery biopsy was performed without complications, though results were pending at discharge. The patient’s vision returned to baseline, and she was discharged home with home health services, with instructions to follow up on biopsy results and medication management.
